title: Mass on a spring

slow_motion.evidence: No captions, narration, or visual cues indicate slow motion

subjects.description: small red rectangular block attached to the bottom of the vertical spring

observation.what_happens: A small red block attached to a vertical white spring oscillates up and down in the center of the frame. The motion is already underway at the start and continues bouncing throughout the clip without being caught or stopping.

calibration.note: no scale: lengths are in pixels

reasoning: The s channel shows ~1.6 s vertical oscillation around ~110 pix with peaks falling 217 to 195 and troughs rising, so a damped oscillator. x is noise, so motion is 1D along s. Candidates go from ideal to viscous to air-drag and dry-friction losses to test the decay shape on hidden data.

law.title: Spring with viscous damping
law.summary: A spring bounces while smooth sticky friction slowly steals its energy.

fitted.title: Spring with viscous damping
fitted.summary: A spring bounces while smooth sticky friction slowly steals its energy.

candidates.ifItWins: The amplitude shrinks exponentially because of smooth viscous friction from air and the spring.

law.title: Damped spring with dry friction
law.summary: A damped spring that also rubs with constant friction like a squeaky coil.

fitted.title: Damped spring with dry friction
fitted.summary: A damped spring that also rubs with constant friction like a squeaky coil.

candidates.ifItWins: Energy loss is partly constant rubbing that makes the height shrink in a straight line rather than fading exponentially.

law.title: Damped spring with air drag
law.summary: A damped spring where fast motion feels extra push-back from the air.

fitted.title: Damped spring with air drag
fitted.summary: A damped spring where fast motion feels extra push-back from the air.

candidates.ifItWins: Fast motion feels extra air resistance that grows with speed squared, not just smooth friction.

law.title: Ideal undamped spring
law.summary: A mass bounces forever on a perfect spring with no friction.

fitted.title: Ideal undamped spring
fitted.summary: A mass bounces forever on a perfect spring with no friction.

candidates.ifItWins: The oscillation amplitude does not truly decay and the decay seen is noise, so a perpetual textbook spring is enough.

law.title: Textbook projectile (no air)
law.summary: Moves at constant horizontal speed while gravity pulls it down at a constant rate.

fitted.title: Textbook projectile (no air)

critique.finding: The block settles around {s_eq} and bounces with spring rate {omega}. A gentle drag {gamma} slowly shrinks each swing.
critique.headline: Spring block keeps bouncing as light damping fades motion
critique.why_it_won: The gentle viscous drag alone explains the slow fade, while added dry rubbing does nothing extra.

headline: Spring block keeps bouncing as light damping fades motion
finding: The block settles around 111 ± 0.018 pix and bounces with spring rate 4 ± 1.82e-4 1/s. A gentle drag 0.12 ± 3.64e-4 1/s slowly shrinks each swing.

eyeball.confidence: low-medium, rough visual estimate from ~2.1 s period and slow amplitude decay
eyeball.law_in_words: Damped vertical spring-mass: position along track oscillates about equilibrium s_eq with damped angular frequency ~omega, envelope decaying as exp(-gamma*t/2), i.e. acceleration = -omega^2*(s-s_eq) - gamma*velocity.
